title: The Branch from Jesse
summary: The prophecy describes a rod and branch from Jesse, and the Spirit of the Lord resting upon him.

explicit_facts.text: A rod comes from the stem of Jesse, and a branch grows from his roots.
The Spirit of the Lord rests upon him, with wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The branch may be shown as a symbolic image of the prophecy.
unspecified_visual_details: The figure’s identity and appearance, the branch’s appearance, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse
and a branch shall grow out of his roots.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses are prophetic language, not a present witnessed event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the figure’s identity or appearance, or depict the Spirit in an unmentioned visible form.

title: Righteous Judgment
summary: The prophecy describes the figure’s discernment, equitable judgment, and righteousness.

explicit_facts.text: He understands in the fear of the Lord and does not judge by sight or reprove by hearing.
He judges the poor righteously and reproves the meek with equity; the rod of his mouth smites the earth, and his lips’ breath slays the wicked.
Righteousness and faithfulness are described as girdles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: These teachings may be conveyed symbolically rather than as literal action.
unspecified_visual_details: The figure’s appearance and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: with righteousness shall he judge the poor
and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The rod of his mouth and breath are prophetic figures of speech, not a narrated combat scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal violence or invent the figure’s identity or appearance.

title: Creatures at Peace
summary: The prophecy pictures animals dwelling and feeding together, with a little child leading them.

explicit_facts.text: A wolf dwells with a lamb; a leopard lies with a kid; a calf, young lion, and fatling are together; a little child leads them.
A cow and bear feed, their young lie down together, and a lion eats straw like an ox.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The animals may be depicted peacefully together as described.
unspecified_visual_details: The animals’ and child’s appearances, and the landscape, are unspecified.

narration.text: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb
and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic imagery, not a present witnessed event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add animals, people, or a named location.

title: No Harm in the Holy Mountain
summary: The prophecy describes children near serpents without harm and declares that nothing will hurt or destroy in the holy mountain.

explicit_facts.text: A suckling child plays on the hole of the asp, and a weaned child puts a hand on the cockatrice’s den.
Nothing shall hurt or destroy in the holy mountain, and the earth shall be full of knowledge of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The children and serpents may be shown in a peaceful setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The children’s and serpents’ appearances and the mountain terrain are unspecified.

narration.text: They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain
for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic imagery, not a present witnessed event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show injury or add details of danger beyond the stated imagery.

title: An Ensign for the People
summary: The root of Jesse stands as an ensign sought by the Gentiles; his rest is glorious.

explicit_facts.text: The root of Jesse stands as an ensign for the people; the Gentiles seek to it, and his rest is glorious.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The ensign may be represented symbolically without specifying its design.
unspecified_visual_details: The figure’s appearance, the ensign’s design, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: there shall be a root of Jesse
which shall stand for an ensign of the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic language, not a present witnessed gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the figure’s appearance or the ensign’s markings.

title: The Remnant Gathered
summary: The prophecy describes the Lord recovering a remnant from named regions and gathering Israel’s outcasts and Judah’s dispersed.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord sets his hand a second time to recover his people’s remnant from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.
He sets up an ensign for the nations, assembles Israel’s outcasts, and gathers Judah’s dispersed from the four corners of the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The gathering may be represented symbolically without specifying a route or assembly place.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s appearance, the Lord’s manner of acting, the ensign’s design, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: shall assemble the outcasts of Israel
and gather together the dispersed of Judah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic future events, not a present-tense narrated gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the Lord’s appearance, details of the named regions, or a specific gathering scene.

title: Ephraim and Judah
summary: The prophecy says Ephraim’s envy will depart and that Ephraim and Judah will no longer vex or envy one another.

explicit_facts.text: Ephraim’s envy departs, Judah’s adversaries are cut off, Ephraim does not envy Judah, and Judah does not vex Ephraim.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching may be represented symbolically, without staging a specific encounter.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether Ephraim and Judah are represented as individuals or groups, and their appearance and setting, are unspecified.

narration.text: and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic language, not a narrated present conflict or reconciliation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a battle or identify specific people as Ephraim or Judah.

title: The Nations and the Remnant
summary: The prophecy describes them turning west and prevailing over named neighboring peoples.

explicit_facts.text: They fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the west, spoil those of the east together, lay their hand upon Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon obey them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The verse may be represented symbolically without inventing a specific battle.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity of “they,” the peoples’ appearances, and the locations are unspecified.

narration.text: and the children of Ammon shall obey them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic summary, not a narrated present battle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign “they” an identity or invent a specific combat event.

title: The Way Through the Waters
summary: The prophecy describes the Egyptian sea and a river’s seven streams, so people may cross dry-shod, and promises a highway for the remnant from Assyria.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord destroys the tongue of the Egyptian sea and shakes his hand over the river with a mighty wind, smiting it into seven streams so people go over dry-shod.
A highway shall be for the remnant left from Assyria, as it was for Israel when coming out of Egypt.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The seven streams and dry crossing may be presented as symbolic prophetic imagery.
unspecified_visual_details: The river’s identity, the people’s appearance, the highway’s form, and the Lord’s appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: with his mighty wind he shall shake his hand over the river
and make men go over dry shod.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic future events, not a present crossing. The exodus is a comparison, not a scene occurring here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the exodus as a present event, identify the river, or invent the Lord’s appearance.
